# CANDIDATE: RIBBON_COMPRESSION_BREAKOUT_VOL_FILTER

**Filed:** 2026-07-09  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** new_trigger  
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

When the EMA ribbon compresses tightly (ribbon width < 0.02 for three consecutive 1-minute bars), a subsequent breakout on above-average volume captures the release of compressed volatility and often trends. This setup aims to capture that edge by entering long (or short) at the close of the breakout bar with a structured exit to manage risk and let runners ride.

## Mechanism

Calculate ribbon width as (8-EMA – 21-EMA) / ATR(14). If ribbon width stays below 0.02 for three consecutive 1-minute bars, and the next bar closes above the high of the third compression bar (for longs) or below its low (for shorts) with volume > 1.3× the average volume of the preceding ten bars, then enter long (or short) at the close of that breakout bar. Exit: Stop placed at the opposite extreme of the three-bar compression zone (low of zone for longs, high for shorts); target 1 at 2× ATR from entry, runner using a trailing stop of 15% below the highest close since entry (for longs) or analogous for shorts.
